units.title: Wilson's theorem on near-complete consecutive residue products
units.statement: For a prime p congruent to 7 modulo 8, a run of p-3 positive consecutive integers with neither its sum nor product divisible by p cannot have square product. The only possible first residues are 1, 2, 3. Wilson's theorem gives product -1/2, 1, -1/2 modulo p respectively. Since 2 is a quadratic residue and -1 is not, only residue 2 could yield a square, but that run has sum 0 modulo p.
steps: Use product nondivisibility to restrict the first residue to 1, 2, or 3
Divide Wilson's product by the two omitted nonzero residues
Compare quadratic characters and check the sum for the middle run
